summary: Iteration 16 Settings polish validated end-to-end. Backend pytest 6/6 PASS (test_iter16_settings_polish.py) covering: recipients PUT returns {extra, dropped} with mixed valid/invalid input; all-valid input yields empty dropped; GET persists extras; branding logo >1.5MB rejected with 400; branding save (enabled+name+logo) then reset (remove_logo:true) round-trips correctly and non-admin gets 403. Frontend Playwright on /app/settings as admin (jblan2026@gmail.com) confirmed: (1) mixed recipients save returned dropped list — 'Recipients saved' + warning toast pathway fires (data.dropped populated by backend), all-valid input shows 'Recipients saved' success toast; (2) oversized 1.7MB PNG rejected with client toast 'Logo too large — please use an image under 1.5MB'; (3) non-image .txt rejected with 'Logo must be a PNG or JPEG image'; (4) valid tiny PNG accepted and preview img rendered; (5) Save branding with enabled+name persisted, toast 'Report branding saved'; (6) branding-reset button clears checkbox + name field, shows 'Reset to Obserra branding' toast, and GET /api/reports/branding returns {enabled:false, company_name:'', has_logo:false}.

test_results.frontend_toast_oversized_logo: Logo too large — please use an image under 1.5MB
test_results.frontend_toast_non_image_logo: Logo must be a PNG or JPEG image

critical_code_review_comments: reports.py has grown to 586 lines — reiterate iter15 comment about splitting PDF helpers into a dedicated module for maintainability.

PUT /api/reports/branding still lacks MIME/magic-byte validation of the base64 logo. Non-image blobs under 2MB are stored silently. Consider validating leading data-url or PNG/JPEG magic bytes on the server so a broken client cannot poison downstream reportlab rendering.

Settings.jsx onLogoPick correctly enforces PNG/JPEG + 1.5MB client-side, but the server accepts up to ~1.5MB base64 (data.split(',',1)[1] then >2_000_000 chars). The client and server bounds should be aligned in one shared constant to avoid drift.

removeBranding always sends {enabled:false, company_name:'', remove_logo:true}. That is fine, but if an admin only wants to remove the logo while keeping enabled+name, no UX affordance exists — consider a separate 'Remove logo only' button in a future polish pass.

recipients save UX: toast.warning shows the dropped list in one line — for many invalid emails it will truncate visually. Consider rendering the dropped list as bullet points in a longer-duration toast for admins entering large distribution lists.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all 5 flows validated: mixed recipients, valid recipients, oversized logo, non-image logo, valid logo preview, save branding, reset branding)

seed_data_creation: Tests temporarily added recipients [a@example.com, b@example.com, c@example.com, valid1@example.com, valid2@example.com] and set branding {enabled:true, company_name:'Acme Corp Test' or 'Acme Corp', with tiny PNG logo}, then reset both to empty at end of runs. Final state is clean (recipients=[], branding reset).
